images.seen: A Nguni cow facing the camera on dew-heavy pasture, the rest of the herd and the trees fading into thick white fog. Tuesday.
lines: The herd is all here; the fog is just rationing them one at a time.
Visibility is down to one cow.
The farm goes on past that white wall; the cows are taking that on faith.

images.seen: A suburban street at blue pre-dawn with fog thickening down the road, three amber streetlamps fading into it, wet tar. Friday.
lines: Three streetlights in and the street gives up; the fog holds the rest.
The fog rolled in at three and started deleting the neighbourhood from the far end.
The streetlights are trying their best.

images.seen: A modern house at dawn with one warm-lit window cutting a long beam through dense fog, dark garden below. Wednesday.
lines: One lit window is taking on the whole fog, and losing beautifully.
The fog is thick enough to hold a beam of kitchen light like a solid object.

images.seen: A schoolboy in a hi-vis vest and backpack waiting at the curb, the street swallowed by fog, one faint pair of headlights deep in the mist. Monday.
lines: The hi-vis is doing exactly what it was bought for this morning.
Those headlights have been 'almost here' for two full minutes of fog.
Fog like this turns every school run into an act of faith and reflective tape.
